NumberWordFormatter.__init__:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Initializes fixed number-to-words lookup tables for ones, teens, tens, thousand groups, and abbreviated suffixes." __init__]
    [INPUTS]
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Assign to self.NUMBER the ones-word lookup table where index 0 is an empty string, index 1 is 'ONE', index 2 is 'TWO', index 3 is 'THREE', index 4 is 'FOUR', index 5 is 'FIVE', index 6 is 'SIX', index 7 is 'SEVEN', index 8 is 'EIGHT', and index 9 is 'NINE'. RESULT self.NUMBER]
            [COMMAND Assign to self.NUMBER_TEEN the teen-word lookup table where index 0 is 'TEN', index 1 is 'ELEVEN', index 2 is 'TWELVE', index 3 is 'THIRTEEN', index 4 is 'FOURTEEN', index 5 is 'FIFTEEN', index 6 is 'SIXTEEN', index 7 is 'SEVENTEEN', index 8 is 'EIGHTEEN', and index 9 is 'NINETEEN'. RESULT self.NUMBER_TEEN]
            [COMMAND Assign to self.NUMBER_TEN the tens-word lookup table where index 0 is 'TEN', index 1 is 'TWENTY', index 2 is 'THIRTY', index 3 is 'FORTY', index 4 is 'FIFTY', index 5 is 'SIXTY', index 6 is 'SEVENTY', index 7 is 'EIGHTY', and index 8 is 'NINETY'. RESULT self.NUMBER_TEN]
            [COMMAND Assign to self.NUMBER_MORE the scale-word lookup table where index 0 is an empty string, index 1 is 'THOUSAND', index 2 is 'MILLION', and index 3 is 'BILLION'. RESULT self.NUMBER_MORE]
            [COMMAND Assign to self.NUMBER_SUFFIX the abbreviated suffix lookup table where index 0 is 'k', index 1 is 'w', index 2 is an empty string, index 3 is 'm', index 4 is an empty string, index 5 is an empty string, index 6 is 'b', index 7 is an empty string, index 8 is an empty string, index 9 is 't', index 10 is an empty string, index 11 is an empty string, index 12 is 'p', index 13 is an empty string, index 14 is an empty string, and index 15 is 'e'. RESULT self.NUMBER_SUFFIX]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.format:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Null-safe formatter that returns the formatted string representation of non-None input and an empty string for None." format]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> x </REF>: any "The value to format; may be None."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> result </REF>: string "The formatted string returned by self.format_string, or an empty string when x is None."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Evaluate whether x is not None. RESULT condition_result]
            [COMMAND If condition_result is true, convert x to a string with str(x), call self.format_string on that string, and return the result. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: x is None]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return an empty string. RESULT result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.format_string:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts a decimal input string into check-style amount words by processing the integer part in three-digit groups and optionally appending cents, then returns the value ending with ONLY or ZERO ONLY." format_string]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> x </REF>: text "Input decimal number as a string."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> return_value </REF>: text "Formatted amount in words ending with ONLY or ZERO ONLY."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Split the input x on '.', append an empty string, take only the first two components, and assign the first component to lstr and the second to rstr. RESULT lstr, rstr]
            [COMMAND Reverse lstr and assign the result to lstrrev. RESULT lstrrev]
            [COMMAND Initialize a as a list of five empty strings. RESULT a]
            [COMMAND If len(lstrrev) % 3 equals 1, append "00" to lstrrev; else if len(lstrrev) % 3 equals 2, append "0" to lstrrev; otherwise leave lstrrev unchanged. RESULT lstrrev]
            [COMMAND Initialize lm to the empty string. RESULT lm]
            [COMMAND For each integer i from 0 through floor(len(lstrrev)/3)-1 inclusive, set a[i] to the reverse of the three-character slice lstrrev[3*i:3*i+3]. RESULT a[i]]
            [COMMAND Within the for loop over i, if a[i] is not exactly "000", set lm to trans_three(a[i]) + " " + parse_more(i) + " " + lm; otherwise append trans_three(a[i]) to lm. RESULT lm]
            [COMMAND After the loop, if rstr is truthy, set xs to the f-string "AND CENTS " followed by trans_two(rstr) and a trailing space; otherwise set xs to "" without calling trans_two. RESULT xs]
            [COMMAND If lm.strip() is truthy, return the concatenation of lm.strip(), a single space, xs, and "ONLY". RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: lm.strip() is falsy after the loop and xs computation.]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the literal string "ZERO ONLY". RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.trans_two:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts a one- or two-digit numeric string into its English word representation by first zero-padding to at least two characters and then selecting among single-digit, teen, exact-tens, and compound tens-and-ones forms." trans_two]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> s </REF>: string "Numeric string to convert; if it is shorter than two characters, it is left-padded with zeros."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> return_value </REF>: string "The English word or phrase corresponding to the input value."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Pad s on the left with zeros to width 2 using s.zfill(2) and rebind the result to s; if s is already at least two characters long, it remains unchanged. RESULT s]
            [COMMAND Evaluate the conditional branches in the order provided and execute the first matching branch, returning its result immediately. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: After zfill, s[0] == '0' (covers '00' through '09').]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return self.NUMBER[int(s[-1])], using the last digit converted to an integer as the list index. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: After zfill and only if the first branch did not match, s[0] == '1' (covers '10' through '19').]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return self.NUMBER_TEEN[int(s) - 10], converting s to an integer and subtracting 10 to obtain the teen list index. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: After zfill and only if the previous branches did not match, s[1] == '0' (covers exact tens '20', '30', ..., '90').]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return self.NUMBER_TEN[int(s[0]) - 1], converting the first character to an integer, subtracting 1, and using that value as the list index. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: After zfill and only if none of the previous branches matched (covers compound values '21' through '99' excluding exact tens).]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return self.NUMBER_TEN[int(s[0]) - 1] followed by a single space ' ' and self.NUMBER[int(s[-1])] to form the tens word followed by the ones word. RESULT return_value]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.trans_three:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Converts a three-digit group string into English hundred-unit words by handling leading-zero groups, exact hundreds, and hundreds with a two-digit remainder." trans_three]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> s </REF>: string "A non-empty three-character digit group string; the method immediately accesses the first character s[0] and the remainder s[1:]."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> trans_three_result </REF>: string "The converted English representation for the three-digit group, delegating leading-zero groups to trans_two and otherwise formatting with HUNDRED and optional AND."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Evaluate the conditional chain over s to select one of three return paths: leading-zero delegation, exact hundreds, or hundreds with a two-digit remainder. RESULT selected_path]
            [COMMAND Return the result produced by the selected path. RESULT trans_three_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: When s[0] equals the string "0"]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return self.trans_two(s[1:]) immediately, bypassing HUNDRED formatting. RESULT trans_three_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: Else when s[1:] equals the string "00"]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the formatted string composed of self.NUMBER[int(s[0])] followed by " HUNDRED". RESULT trans_three_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

    [ALTERNATIVE_FLOW: Otherwise]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the formatted string composed of self.NUMBER[int(s[0])] followed by " HUNDRED AND " and self.trans_two(s[1:]). RESULT trans_three_result]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_ALTERNATIVE_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
NumberWordFormatter.parse_more:
[DEFINE_WORKER: "Returns the element stored in the instance attribute NUMBER_MORE at the provided index or key i." parse_more]
    [INPUTS]
        <REF> i </REF>: object "Index or key used to select an element from the instance attribute NUMBER_MORE."
    [END_INPUTS]

    [OUTPUTS]
        <REF> selected_element </REF>: object "The element from NUMBER_MORE located at index or key i."
    [END_OUTPUTS]

    [MAIN_FLOW]
        [SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
            [COMMAND Return the element selected by subscripting the instance attribute NUMBER_MORE with the provided index or key i. RESULT selected_element]
        [END_SEQUENTIAL_BLOCK]
    [END_MAIN_FLOW]

[END_WORKER]
